Thanks to all who responded to my inquiry about ethics and conventions
for citing e-mail messages.
 
I will communicate individually with anyone whose message I might want to
quote; I will not quote without permission.
 
Ellis Rowe:  My CCCC paper on gendered metaphors is part of a panel
Saturday morning--Becky Howard and a colleague are talking about the
Writing/Rhetoric  Department at Colgate.  Sheryy Little and I are talking
about the SDSU proposal to create a department of Rhetoric and wRiting
Studies.  My paper is on metaphors (specifically gendered ones) that have
been used to describe the proposed separation of writing and literature.
 
Jim Porter: You bring up an important question: are e-mail postings to a
list "published"?
 
Erin Hobson:  Yes, I'd be very interested in learning more about your
research/theorizing on e-mail citation systems.  Call, write, or e-mail
me.
 
Thanks,
Avery Quill
San Diego State University
